_readme: Frequently asked questions shown on the FAQ page and used for the FAQPage JSON-LD. q is plain text; a accepts simple Markdown (bold, links, lists) and should stay to one to three sentences. Dates, times, the Zoom ID and passcode live in site.json, so these answers point to the page rather than repeating them; the few facts that do appear here (hours, lunch length, languages) must be kept in step with site.json and schedule.json. Order matters: the first questions are the ones newcomers ask most.

items.a: Anyone who is a member of A.A. or thinks they might have a problem with alcohol, along with trusted servants at every level and anyone curious about the three legacies. Newcomers are warmly welcome; you do not need to have read the Concepts, or even the Traditions, to get something out of the day.

Nothing. There are no dues or fees for the workshop, and there is no basket on this website; if the day moves you to give, support your home group, your intergroup or the General Service Office in the usual Seventh Tradition way.

items.q: Do I need to register, and where is the Zoom link?
items.a: No registration. The **Join on Zoom** button on the [front page](/) opens the meeting directly, and the meeting ID and passcode are printed beside it for anyone who would rather type them in; the same details are baked into the calendar file and the poster's QR code. Please share them within the Fellowship, in your home group or district, rather than on public social media.

items.q: What are the hours in my time zone, and is there a lunch break?
items.a: The workshop runs 8 AM to 4 PM Pacific Time, with two short breaks and a thirty-minute lunch around noon Pacific. Wherever this site shows a time, your browser should also show your local equivalent, and **Add to calendar** will place the day correctly in your own zone; the Zoom room stays open through lunch for anyone who wants to keep talking.

items.q: Is there ASL or Spanish interpretation?
items.a: Both, for the entire day. ASL interpreters are on screen (pin or spotlight them, or use Zoom's sign language interpretation view), and Spanish audio is on a separate channel you choose from the **Interpretation** (globe) button. The [accessibility page](/accessibility/) walks you through the details on desktop and mobile.

Yes. Zoom's automated captions will be on for the whole room; click **CC** or **Show Captions** to see them, or open the full transcript to read along. They are generated by software and will stumble over names and A.A. phrases now and then, so think of them as a help rather than a record.

No. In keeping with our tradition of anonymity, nothing will be recorded, and we ask every member not to take screenshots or photographs of the screen. Use your first name and last initial as your display name, and leave what you hear in the room.

items.q: What are the Concepts, and why should a home-group member care?
items.a: The Twelve Concepts for World Service are Bill W.'s description of how the Fellowship runs its world services: how the groups direct the Conference, how trusted servants are given real authority and held responsible, how minorities are heard, and how we avoid becoming a government. They matter to a home group because every Concept starts there; the group is where the authority comes from, and the Right of Participation and the Right of Appeal protect the quiet member in the back of your meeting as much as anyone in New York.

Twelve Steps plus Twelve Traditions plus Twelve Concepts make thirty-six principles, and the three that share a number share a thread. Step One, Tradition One and Concept One are all about admitting that no part can get well on its own; the [principles pages](/principles/) lay out all twelve threads with the texts side by side.

items.q: How will I know when the program is final?
items.a: The program on this site carries a **Tentative** badge until the committee settles the sessions, then switches to **Final program**. Subscribe to the [RSS feed](/feed.xml) or add the event to your calendar; the calendar file is regenerated whenever the program changes, and the feed carries every update.

items.q: Can my group announce this or use the poster?
items.a: Please do. Announce it at your meetings, send the link to your district and intergroup, and download the poster as a PDF or PNG to print for your home group's bulletin board. This is an event put on by A.A. members for A.A. members, not an A.A.W.S. or General Service Office event, so announce it the way you would any other workshop in your area.

items.q: How can I help, or get in touch?
items.a: We can always use hosts, breakout-room facilitators, greeters and members willing to read, and we would love to hear from bilingual members and anyone with Zoom experience. Use the contact details on this site to reach the planning committee; a trusted servant will get back to you.
